s.t:
You will lay out work from blueprints, sketches, drawings and oral instructions.
You will utilize trade methods and processes to ensure conformance to requirements.
You will Install wireways, cable racks, and associated cabling to interconnect ships power, communications, lighting, fire control, instrumentation and other electrical systems.
You will troubleshoot faulty systems/circuitry to identify problem areas and initiates action to commence repairs.
Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time.Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below.This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job.

Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible. The Screen-out Element for this position is: ABILITY TO WORK WITHOUT MORE THAN NORMAL SUPERVISION such as: Ability to read and interpret blueprints, specifications, sketches, and electrical schematics.

Proficiency in laying out work, operating various machines, and using test equipment such as multimeters, meggers, and ammeters. A working knowledge of shipboard electrical installation techniques and processes. Ability to operate a variety of power and hand tools (e.g., drill presses, hydraulic punches, grinders).

A solid mathematical background and the ability to apply electrical trade theory to perform both routine and complex work. Ability to utilize systems such as power and lighting, alarm systems, and motor controllers.

Ability to understand electrical safety practices and the ability to follow all prescribed safety rules, especially concerning energy isolation (lockout/tagout). Ability to apply electrical theory to troubleshoot faulty circuits and identify problem areas.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/federal-wage-system-qualifications/#url=List-of-Approved-Job-Elements Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
To support this ambitious goal, we are seeking an Electrical Test Technician to join our Electrical Integration & Test Team in Munich. You will be responsible for the assembly, integration, maintenance, and modification of electrical test systems used throughout the development, verification, and validation of spacecraft subsystems and avionics equipment.
You will play a key role in building and maintaining custom test racks, integrating commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and custom-designed hardware, and supporting engineers during test campaigns. Working closely with electrical, avionics, and system engineers, you will help ensure our test infrastructure meets the highest standards of quality, reliability, and safety.

s.h: In your role as Electrical Test Technician, you will
s.t:
Assemble, wire, and integrate electrical test racks and ground support equipment
Perform wiring and interconnections between COTS equipment and custom-designed hardware
Manufacture, route, label, and install electrical harnesses and cables according to engineering documentation
Interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical drawings to perform integration and troubleshooting activities
Support electrical integration, verification, and test campaigns across multiple projects
Perform inspections, modifications, and repairs on electrical assemblies and test equipment
Assist in the installation, replacement, and rework of electronic components on PCBs when required
Execute continuity, insulation, and basic electrical verification tests on assemblies and harnesses
Maintain accurate documentation of wiring modifications, test setups, and configuration changes
Support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations on electrical and test systems

s.h: You and your team will be in charge of
s.t:
Building and maintaining reliable electrical test infrastructures for spacecraft development and qualification activities
Integrating a wide variety of electrical equipment, including power supplies, measurement devices, automation components, and custom electronics
Ensuring all rack assemblies and wiring installations comply with internal standards and safety requirements
Supporting engineers during test setup preparation, execution, and troubleshooting activities
Contributing to the continuous improvement of test equipment, assembly processes, and documentation practices
Maintaining high levels of workmanship, quality, and configuration control across all electrical integration activities
Ensuring electrical installations are safe, maintainable, and suitable for demanding aerospace test environments

Technical diploma, vocational qualification, or equivalent experience in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Mechatronics, Industrial Automation, or a related field
Proven hands-on experience in electrical assembly, wiring, and integration activities
Ability to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation
Experience assembling and wiring electrical cabinets, racks, or industrial control systems
Knowledge of cable and wire selection principles, including preliminary conductor sizing based on electrical loads and installation constraints
Familiarity with common industrial automation components such as relays, contactors, circuit breakers, terminal blocks, sensors, power supplies, and I/O modules
Experience using standard electrical test equipment, including multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, and continuity testers
Strong troubleshooting skills and a structured, methodical approach to problem-solving
High attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship
Fluent in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced environment
Nice-to-Have Skills
Experience with aerospace, automotive, railway, or other highly regulated industries
Experience performing PCB assembly, component replacement, soldering, and electronic rework
Familiarity with low-voltage DC power distribution systems
Knowledge of cable harness manufacturing and connector assembly standards
Experience working with custom-built test equipment and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) environments
Ability to design rack front panels and front-end layouts for custom test systems
Familiarity with CAD tools for electrical or mechanical design documentation
Understanding of configuration management and documentation control processes
Why you should join us!
What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:
We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind
We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them
We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?

Diagnose and troubleshoot signal integrity issues, intermittent connections, grounding problems, and EMI/EMC-related effects
Maintain, modify and repair test equipment wiring, connectors, harnesses and supporting electrical infrastructure
Maintain accurate wiring schematics, cable lists, test logs, and configuration documentation
Collaborate with HIL engineers, System Engineers and software teams to support test readiness and failure investigations
Contribute to continuous improvement of HIL hardware design, build process and safety practices
What we would love to see from you

Technical diploma or bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechatronics, or related field
3+ years of hands-on electrical work, preferably in aerospace or high-reliability/safety-critical environments
Demonstrated experience assembling and wiring HiL test benches, racks, or complex test setups
Strong ability to interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, pin‑outs, and harness drawings
Familiarity with aerospace or industrial standards (e.g., ECSS, MIL‑STD, IPC, or equivalent)
Practical experience in cable and harness fabrication , including crimping, soldering, heat‑shrinking, and connector assembly
Proficiency with electrical and electronic test equipment , such as multimeters, power supplies, oscilloscopes, signal generators, and harness testers
Solid understanding of EMI/EMC best practices , grounding concepts, and shielding technique
Experience with spacecraft avionics, GSE, or propulsion test systems is a plus
High attention to detail, strong workmanship standards, and a safety‑first mindset
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a multidisciplinary team

Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong analysis and problem-solving skills
Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks
Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done

Key Tasks

Perform sub-assembly, final assembly, and repair tasks on aircraft, payloads, and associated components in accordance with work in-strictions and quality standards.
Execute scheduled and unscheduled maintenance activities both at the Swiss headquarters and during international deployments.
Conduct inspections, installations, removals, replacements, and functional testing of subsystems and ground support equipment (GSE).

Support pre-flight and post-flight inspections, system preparation, and maintenance, ensuring all work is completed, documented, and signed off correctly.
Prepare and maintain aircraft, Ground Control Stations (GCS), data transmission systems, and payloads for flight missions.
Assist remote pilots and manage ground movements during flight operations.

Ensure full traceability and documentation of all tasks performed, including inspection and testing of incoming goods and parts.
Comply with safety standards, internal quality protocols, work instructions, and regulatory requirements (including handling Dangerous Goods).
Maintain all GSE in operational condition to support daily flight and test activities.
Other Tasks

Perform fault diagnosis using appropriate test equipment and support root cause analysis and implementation of corrective actions for sys-tem failures or malfunctions.
Contribute suggestions for product and process improvements based on operational experience.

Act as a technician instructor for internal and/or external training sessions.
Collaborate proactively with engineering, logistics, and operations teams to ensure seamless mission support.

Working independently and responsibly. Perform task tasks as described above. Proactive communication when issues arise, or help is needed.
Compliance according to ANAVIA’ employment contract, compliance with company’ safety instructions and employee’ safety requirements, compliance with employers’ quality manual, work instructions and cor-responding process specifications and instructions.
Assure 5s behavior to drive clean, safe and efficient work processes.
International travel requires up to 50% of employee’ working hours.
Your profile

Completed technical education (e.g., in mechanical, electrical, or aerospace engineering).
Minimum 7 years of experience as an aircraft technician (manned and/or unmanned).
Proven understanding of aircraft assembly, system integration, and maintenance procedures.
Strong diagnostic skills and hands-on experience with technical test equipment.
Strong English communication skills, both verbal and written.
Working knowledge of operational risk management practices.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite and documentation tools.
Valid driver’s license.

s.h: You will perform the normal duties of an Electrician Mechanic.
s.t:
You will perform non-supervisory work and directing the work of three or more mechanics of the trade, and/or any additional helpers, workers, and apprentices assigned.
You will provide general direction on how to perform the work and demonstrate initiative to get the job started.
You will check the progress of jobs and resolve delays when possible.
You will train electricians and military technicians in all aspects of the electrical trade.
Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below.

This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job. Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible. The Screen-out Element for this position is: Ability to Lead or Supervise.

Applicants must meet the requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Job Qualification Handbook for Trades and Labor Occupations.

Additional qualification information can be found at: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/federal-wage-system-qualifications/#url=List-of-Approved-Job-Elements Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Installs, modifies, inspects, tests and repairs electrical distribution lines, secondary lines, substations, transformers, breakers, regulators, insulators, lightning arrestors, switches, fuses and similar equipment.
Works on underground and overhead primary distribution systems of up to 115,000 volts.
Troubleshoots distribution systems and equipment using devices such as voltmeters, ohmmeters, phase meters, meggers, underground cable locators and thermal imaging cameras.
Checks voltage of secondary terminals, and makes repairs to defective, loose, or corroded connections.
Works from building plans, drawings, and manuals to plan, layout, determine wire, fixture and equipment type and size, balance the load, and ensure the proper and safe operating of electrical lines, circuits, systems, equipment and controls.
Performs work associated with installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and calibrating complex electronic equipment such as, protective relays, reclosures, tap changers, regulators, battery chargers, and circuit breakers.
Operates boom crane devices at various outdoor locations where maneuverability is restricted due to close proximity of high voltage lines and equipment and accuracy is critical.
Periodically inspects all transformers, lines, streetlights, substations, manholes, underground cables, and arresters.
Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected.

See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities.

Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Domestic Defense Industrial Base/Major Range and Test Facilities Base Civilian Personnel Workforce Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social).

You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. There is no specific length of training or experience required.

However, you must be able to demonstrate, through experience shown in your written application materials that you possess the sufficient knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the work of this position without more than normal supervision.

Minimum Qualifications (Screen Out Element): Ability to do the work of an Electrician (High Voltage/Motor Vehicle Operator) without more than normal supervision.

The work of the position normally includes: (1) I can work from building plans, blueprints, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings, and electrical maintenance and repair manuals to plan, layout, determine wire, fixture and equipment type and size, balance the load, and insure the proper and safe operating of electrical lines, circuits, systems, equipment and controls.

Failure to meet this Screen Out Element will result in an ineligible rating.

Ability To Do The Work Of The Position Without More Than Normal Supervision Ability To Use and Maintain Hand Tools (Electrical Work) Ability To Use Electrical Drawings Knowledge of Electrical Equipment Technical Practices (theoretical, precise, artistic) Theory and Instruments (Electrical Electronic) Used in Shop and Trade Practices Trouble shooting (electrical) Physical Efforts - Moderately heavy physical effort is exerted as employee works aloft on poles, at ground level, and in ground trenches or manholes.

Work requires bending, stooping, climbing, and standing for long periods. Coordination of eyes, hands, legs, and body is needed in installing, repairing, and testing electrical equipment in confined spaces such as manholes and overhead structures.

Working Conditions - Works outside most of the time, subject to extremes of weather conditions, which could result in mandatory 24-hour emergency call, and in close proximity to high voltage lines and equipment. Work requires extensive pole climbing with some work in underground facilities.

Subject to death or serious injury by contact with high voltage lines, broken bones in falls from poles, strains from awkward positions, and less serious cuts and bruises when handling tools and materials.

May be required to work in contaminated areas, exposed to hazardous chemicals and toxic fumes requiring the wearing of uncomfortable protective devices including respirators and impermeable rubber suits.

We build the intelligence that lets robots sense, reason, and act in the real world—moving beyond the lab and into everyday industrial settings like warehouses and factories. Our technology closes the automation gaps that traditional systems can’t solve. We are on a mission to redefine how physical work gets done, and we’re looking for curious, bold thinkers to help shape the future of robotics with us.

We are looking for a hands-on electrician or automation technician to support the build, installation, and optimization of our robotic systems. You will be responsible for wiring, testing, and commissioning electrical components both in our lab and on-site. You will collaborate closely with mechanical and software teams to ensure seamless system integration, resolve technical issues, and implement improvements across new and existing systems.

Installation & Integration
Build and wire electrical systems for robotic applications, including cabinets and field wiring.
Support system commissioning in the robotics lab and at customer locations.
Work closely with mechanical and software engineers to ensure correct system integration.
Implement technical improvements and modifications based on project feedback.
Diagnose and resolve electrical faults during development and deployment.

Completed technical training (e.g. State-certified Technician in Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, or Automation) or a comparable vocational qualification (e.g. Electrician, Control Cabinet Builder, Electrical Master)
Certified to perform electrical work (Elektrofachkraft – EFK)
Relevant professional experience in automation or robotics preferred
Willingness to travel: ≈ 25-50%
Skills
Experience with electrical installations, control systems, sensors, and actuators
Hands-on mentality and technical craftsmanship
Basic knowledge of EPLAN/Splan is a plus
Valid Class B driver’s license (EU)

On‑site visit: Meet the team in our office and collaborate on a real challenge similar to the work you’d do here. You’ll also meet a founder; we aim to give you a clear feel for the role and environment.

Installs, modifies connects, inspects, troubleshoots, and repairs overhead and underground primary electrical distribution lines serving the Defense Supply Center Richmond.
Most work is performed on de-energized lines; however, will occasionally be required to work on energized lines under special conditions.
Installs, maintains, and repairs a variety of complete high voltage terminations from cable preparation to conductor and jacket sealing.
Installs and maintains pole and pad mounted transformers and switches.
Maintains street lights and performs tree trimming and cleaning during bad weather.
Answers trouble calls for inside or outside electrical work, makes diagnosis and accomplishes repair or notifies supervisor when major repairs are requested.
Applicants will be rated in accordance with the Office of Personnel Management Qualification Standard for Trades and Labor Occupations.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties at the level for which you are applying.

Emphasis is placed on how you gained the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time, and the required ability or potential to perform the job. Applicants who do not meet the screen-out element (SOE) will be eliminated from further competition.

The SOE and minimum qualifications for this position is: perform the common tasks of the job to be filled but under close supervision, such as work on power cables,transformers, insulators, make electrical connections, splice cables and control equipment such as switches,circuit breakers and panels and, use and maintain various hand and power tools of the trade.

Selective Placement Factor: Incumbent must possess a valid state commercial driver's license (CDL) with class B endorsement.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Physical Effort: Moderately heavy physical effort is exerted as the position works aloft on poles, at ground level, and in ground trenches, or manholes.

Work requires carrying tools, bolts, nuts, and equipment weighing up to 75 pounds, heavy lifting, pulling, and carrying of equipment and material weighing up to 40 pounds and occasionally, they lift or pull heavy cables and equipment weighing more than 50 pounds with the help of weight handling equipment or with assistance from other workers.

They use block and tackle, pulleys, or other lifting devices. They crouch, stand, kneel, and stoop while installing, repairing, or testing electrical equipment in confined spaces such as enclosed switch gear, or in structures such as overhead bus and conduit assemblies.

Workers at the grade 8 level work above ground from aerial bucket trucks and poles, at ground level, and in trenches, or manholes. Work requires bending, stooping, climbing, and standing for long periods while installing, repairing, and testing electrical equipment in manholes and on overhead distribution lines.

Working Conditions: Works outside most of the time, subject to extremes of weather conditions and works with energized high voltage lines and requires work in underground facilities.

Subject to death or injury by contact with high voltage lines, broken bones from falls, strains from awkward positions and less serious cuts and bruises when handling tools and materials.

Lineman is called in at night and/or weekends during severe thunderstorms, heavy winds, or to perform duty in a hazardous location and must make the correct repairs before throwing in the final switch.

Electrical Systems

Assemble and install electrical components using hand tools and soldering equipment.
Perform system functional tests. Repair or replace defective electrical wiring, connectors, and electronic components.
Documentation & Compliance

Ensure compliance with FAA/EASA airworthiness directives and service bulletins.
Safety & Quality Assurance

Conduct pre-flight and post-maintenance inspections.

Ensure all work meets quality standards and regulatory requirements.

Working independently and responsibly. Perform tasks as described above.

Physical: Capable of standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping, and working in awkward positions for extended periods. Manual dexterity and fine motor skills for precision work with small components and soldering. Visual acuity to inspect components, read technical documents, and identify defects. Hearing ability sufficient to detect abnormal sounds during engine runs and equipment operation.
